open_items.detail: The history block carries dated factual claims: Luca Pacioli and double entry in 1494 and the royal charter to the Royal Niger Company in 1886 (line 221); the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria on 1st September, 1965 and the Association of National Accountants of Nigeria on 31st July,1979 as the second professional accounting body (line 225). The regulator and tax-body abbreviations (LSBIR and FBIR at line 165; CBN, NDIC, SEC, CAC and NSE at line 175) and the training-time claim at line 97 (a few months against about five years) are also factual claims. The existing item FA-FACT-T1-DATED-REFERENCES cites older line numbers for these claims (215-223 and 169-179, with the paragraph numbers 217 and 219); in the extract the history block is lines 215-225, the claims are at lines 221 and 225, and the regulators are at lines 165 and 175.
open_items.required_action: Verify each claim against an authoritative primary source through FA-FACT-T1-DATED-REFERENCES, using the line numbers recorded here, and keep the source wording visibly separate from any corrected fact. Do not present any of them as verified in a lesson before that.

open_items.detail: Evaluation question 2 of the second block (line 233, state four duties of an accountant in a business organisation) cannot be answered from the source: duty and duties occur only in the question, and the accounting definition at line 87 lists activities rather than duties.
open_items.required_action: Teacher decides which approved material supplies the duties of an accountant; the bounded lesson task FA-LES-T1-W01-ACCOUNTANT-DUTIES carries that decision. Do not invent a list of duties from the definition.

open_items.detail: Three weekend items cannot be keyed from the taught text alone. Item 3 (line 249, which is not a purpose of financial accounting) offers determining profit (taught at line 195), fixing prices (a competitor's purpose at line 147), credit dealings (a creditor's purpose at lines 135 and 139) and determining cash balance (never taught), so the answer depends on whose purpose is meant. Item 4 (line 251, the fourth stage of the accounting information system) uses the word stage, which occurs only there; the six verbs of the definition at line 87 are not called stages, and counting them gives summarizing, an inference the source does not state. Item 2 (line 247) says financial accounting information while line 99 speaks of accounting records. Items 1 (line 245) and 5 (line 253) point at lines 83 and 221 but no key states it.
open_items.required_action: Teacher or key author decides the expected answer and wording for items 2 to 4 and records the basis; do not mark an option letter as correct from this indexing.
